claims.text: Cold rolling followed by heat treatment can produce a fully recrystallized, fine-grained, single-phase FCC Co33Cr24Ni33V10 alloy.
The untreated fine-grained Co33Cr24Ni33V10 alloy can exhibit a yield strength of approximately 1060 MPa.
The untreated fine-grained Co33Cr24Ni33V10 alloy can exhibit 24.1% uniform elongation.
Dislocation slip and stacking faults govern deformation and strain hardening in the untreated fine-grained Co33Cr24Ni33V10 alloy.
Fine grains and solid-solution strengthening underpin the high yield strength of the untreated Co33Cr24Ni33V10 alloy.
The untreated CoCrNiV-type alloy has high impact-induced energy-release capacity.
Approximately 0.5 at.% oxygen can be incorporated as an interstitial addition in the proposed CoCrNiV-type alloy.
Interstitial oxygen occupies or migrates between interstitial lattice sites.
Interstitial oxygen produces only slight or modest lattice distortion in the proposed alloy.
The oxygen-induced increase in stacking-fault energy suppresses twinning and promotes dislocation glide.
Oxygen stabilizes dislocation and stacking-fault structures in the proposed alloy.
At approximately 0.5 at.% oxygen, detrimental oxide precipitates will not form.
Oxygen addition will increase strain hardening and uniform elongation relative to the untreated alloy.
The oxygen-doped alloy will retain approximately the untreated alloy's high yield strength.
The oxygen-doped alloy will retain the untreated alloy's impact-induced energy-release capacity.
The proposed strength-ductility benefit will persist under both room-temperature quasi-static loading and high-strain-rate impact loading.
The beneficial oxygen effect is restricted to concentrations at or below approximately 0.5 at.%.
Higher oxygen concentrations may cause oxide precipitation, embrittlement, phase instability, or degraded mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The target property alternates between impact-induced energy release and impact-energy absorption. These are distinct quantities, but the experiment treats absorption or release as interchangeable, leaving the energetic outcome ambiguous.
